To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a ruthenium(2+)-bipyridine complex is a more efficient warhead for CALI than a common organic fluorophore and that a general and convenient assay system for evaluating the performance of warheads in CALI has been developed and applied to the evaluation of a variety of warheads.

we have developed a general and convenient method for evaluating the efficiency in living systems of various chromophores for CALI of proteins, that this system has revealed that a ruthenium-based chromophore is markedly more efficient than the commonly used fluorescein, and that we have developed and tested a method to deliver the ruthenium-based warhead into living cells.

(i) a convenient system for the evaluation of the efficiency of chromo- and fluorophores in CALIs has been established, and (ii) Ru(II) bipyridyl complexes are unusually efficient "warheads" for CALI.

the development of a new class of photosensitizing molecules, based on ruthenium(2+) tris-bipyidyl, that can be used for the targeted inactivation of proteins in living cells.
the design and synthesis of new chromophores that can be used to trigger protein disruption.
the development of new and efficient chromophores to enable the CALI of proteins, which will be a powerful tool in the biological research community.

the use of the Ru(II) complex as a "warhead" is an attractive alternative to the use of fluorescein in CALI experiments.

the ruthenium( II) complex is a better warhead than fluorescein, but the latter has the advantage of being a fluorophore and can be used for both CALI and fluorescence microscopy, whereas the former is a non-fluorophore.

Ru(II) bis-tris-bipyridine dication is an excellent chromophore for CALI.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CALI is not limited to the inactivation of proteins in vitro but is also applicable to in vivo systems.
